labels.expectedFinding: Spanish has distinct singular forms of address (tú, usted; vos elsewhere); the Ukrainian prompt «в людини» fixes neither.
With body parts the established use is the definite article (me duele la cabeza), not the possessive (me duele mi cabeza).
«ordenador» is the form used in Spain (computadora/computador are correct elsewhere).
Interrogative adónde and a dónde are both accepted spellings with the same meaning.
«No viene nadie» has the same meaning as «Nadie viene»: nobody comes; the negative word after the verb with no before it is the normal pattern, not a double positive.
After con the pronouns mí and ti take the forms conmigo and contigo.
Numerals ending in un/una agree in gender with the following noun: veintiuna personas, treinta y una personas — not «veintiún/treinta y un personas».
In Ukrainian «апостроф» is the comma-shaped sign written after a consonant (п'ять); the acute mark is «знак наголосу» (акут), so the feedback names the wrong sign.
«акут» is a standard Ukrainian name for the acute sign (СУМ: знак цього наголосу на письмі), so «знак наголосу (акут)» is correct; también is written with the accent.
Existential haber stays singular in compound tenses too: ha habido problemas, not «han habido».
In the 12-hour model the part of the day is given by de la mañana/tarde/noche; without it «a las siete» can be 7:00 or 19:00, and a class at either time is plausible.
la is the feminine singular direct-object pronoun; here it picks up «una de ellas», whose identity the text does not give.
